section_summary: This section assembles several dossiers on alleged Japanese subversion and wartime economic activity, including intercepted correspondence involving C. Fujii, an intelligence note on Li Shengwu, and an extensive censorship analysis of SKF’s Swedish, Japanese, Manchukuoan, and Brazilian operations. The SKF material examines pro-Axis personnel, suspected shipments of chlorate of potash and other war materials to Japan and Manchukuo, and subsequent personnel dismissals in Brazil. Later documents concern suspected Japanese sympathizers or agents Tanji in Tahiti, Ely Widler in Shanghai and Sichuan, and Serge Wittouck in connection with Portuguese Timor.

subfiles.title: Case jacket: Alleged Japanese subversive activities of C. Fujii
subfiles.about: A jacket identifies the file concerning alleged Japanese subversive activities by C. Fujii.
subfiles.summary: Case jacket for alleged Japanese subversive activities of C. Fujii, 1942.

subfiles.title: Index-and-return routing request
subfiles.about: A routing form requests that material be indexed and returned with any previous correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip asking staff to check the file and return it with related correspondence; stamped April 10, 1947.

subfiles.title: Censorship comment on Yamashita’s letter to C. Fujii
subfiles.about: Duplicate censorship sheets summarize a Japanese-language letter from Yamashita in Huancayo to C. Fujii in Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: The letter mentions illness and correspondence with Tashitaro Amano in Panama and H. Kashihara in Lima. Yamashita praises Chiang Kai-shek while declaring that Japan’s unified people and army will win the war and make Japan master of Asia. The original letter was condemned by the censors.

subfiles.title: Case jacket: Li Shengwu
subfiles.about: A jacket opens a case concerning Li Shengwu.
subfiles.summary: Case jacket for Li Shengwu under file 894.20200, preceding an intelligence report on his alleged link to Wang Jingwei's government.

subfiles.title: Intelligence report on Li Shengwu
subfiles.to: FBI; Military Intelligence Service; Department of State
subfiles.about: An intelligence note reports that Li Shengwu represented Wang Jingwei in Europe and may have contacted collaborationist Chinese abroad.
subfiles.summary: Report on Li Shengwu, Wang Jingwei's European representative with headquarters in Berlin, possibly in contact with collaborationist Chinese in London and the U.S.

subfiles.title: File charge-out record
subfiles.about: A later administrative card records charges and due dates for material from the file.
subfiles.summary: File charge-out record with partly legible entries, including Park.

subfiles.title: Case jackets: Alleged subversive activities of SKF Industries
subfiles.about: Two copies of a jacket identify the investigation of alleged Japanese subversive activities involving SKF Industries.
subfiles.summary: The covers open the SKF Industries portion of file 894.20200. The following documents investigate company personnel, political sympathies, and wartime trade.

subfiles.title: SKF enclosure charge slip
subfiles.about: A brief charge slip records an enclosure associated with the SKF file.
subfiles.summary: The page contains a file number, enclosure notation, and clerical fields. It provides no substantive account of the investigation.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting an assessment of SKF officials in Brazil
subfiles.to: United States Embassy, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Acheson asks the embassy for a confidential assessment of SKF officials Wistrand and Hanvik.
subfiles.summary: Acheson asks William Batt for frank comments on allegations that SKF's Brazil managers Wistrand and Hanvik engaged in activities hostile to the U.S.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Rio de Janeiro on pro-Axis sentiment within SKF
subfiles.doc_type: incoming telegram with duplicate file copy
subfiles.from: Jefferson Caffery, United States Embassy, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Caffery reports on pro-Axis sympathies among SKF employees in Brazil and recommends a personnel investigation.
subfiles.summary: Rio telegram: the Swedish minister worries about pro-Axis SKF employees; the Bahia manager was dismissed and the office closed, and the embassy backs an investigator empowered to change personnel.

subfiles.title: Telegram proposing Hugo von Rosen as SKF investigator
subfiles.to: United States Embassy, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: The Department asks whether SKF foreign sales manager Hugo von Rosen should investigate the company’s Brazilian operations.
subfiles.summary: Batt says SKF will send an officer to Brazil and proposes Hugo von Rosen, though the Swedish minister viewed him unfavorably; he asks the ambassador's opinion.

subfiles.title: Telegram opposing Hugo von Rosen’s selection
subfiles.from: Jefferson Caffery, United States Embassy, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Caffery recommends selecting someone other than Hugo von Rosen to investigate SKF Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Caffery notes that the Swedish minister questions von Rosen’s political sympathies. He therefore advises Batt to choose another investigator.

subfiles.title: Instruction to card names
subfiles.about: A short note instructs staff to ensure that the names in the SKF material are indexed on cards.
subfiles.summary: The note contains only a request that the names be carded. It reflects the Department’s indexing procedure for investigative files.

subfiles.title: Censorship analysis of Gösta Guston’s intercepted SKF correspondence
subfiles.doc_type: multi-page censorship intelligence report with duplicate copies
subfiles.to: Gösta Guston, care of K. Guston
subfiles.about: A censorship report analyzes intercepted mail concerning SKF’s international structure, Japanese operations, and wartime trade.
subfiles.summary: The examiner identifies Gösta Birger Thor Guston as a senior SKF-Japan executive and reconstructs connections among SKF-Sweden, SKF-Japan, SKF-Manchukuo, Ekman Foreign Agencies, Norden Export Company, Swedish Match, and Philippine Match. Particular attention is given to a possibly deceptive shipment of 100 tons of chlorate of potash routed through Vladivostok and Yokohama for Japan and Manchukuo. The report argues that SKF companies supplied or manufactured materials important to Japan’s war economy and used contacts with Japanese officials to expedite licenses. It also inventories pro-Axis newspapers and industrial bulletins enclosed in the intercepted correspondence; the examiner’s report itself was completed on April 3, 1942.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch no. 7963 on Hugo von Rosen’s Brazilian investigation
subfiles.from: John F. Simmons, for the Ambassador
subfiles.about: The embassy reports on Hugo von Rosen’s visit to investigate SKF personnel in Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Despatch no. 7963: von Rosen spent two weeks in Brazil investigating SKF personnel, with actions involving Rio de Janeiro and Porto Alegre employees later confirmed as dismissals.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch no. 8916 confirming SKF dismissals
subfiles.from: John F. Simmons, for the Ambassador
subfiles.about: The embassy confirms the dismissal of three SKF Brazil employees following von Rosen’s investigation.
subfiles.summary: Despatch no. 8916: Cia. SKF do Brasil directors report Jensen, Steinberger and Bredemeyer discharged on von Rosen's instructions as of August 1, 1942.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to SKF information in file 862.20232/556A
subfiles.about: A cross-reference directs researchers to another file containing information on possible SKF subversive activities.
subfiles.summary: The note identifies SKF Industries as the subject of relevant information. It points to reference file 862.20232/556A.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to SKF information in file 862.20232/557
subfiles.about: A cross-reference identifies another file containing information on suspected SKF subversive activities.
subfiles.summary: The note names SKF Industries as the subject. The cited reference file is 862.20232/557.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference concerning Guston
subfiles.about: A cross-reference points to another record concerning Guston and SKF Industries.
subfiles.summary: The note associates a Guston entry with the SKF Industries investigation. It cites reference file 858.202.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to SKF information in file 862.20210
subfiles.about: A cross-reference directs users to file 862.20210 for information about SKF Industries.
subfiles.summary: The note concerns possible subversive activities connected with SKF Industries. No individual is named on this particular sheet.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference concerning Henrik Börjeson
subfiles.about: A cross-reference points to information on possible subversive activity involving Henrik Börjeson and SKF Industries.
subfiles.summary: Henrik Börjeson is indexed under the SKF Industries investigation. The referenced material is in file 862.20210.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference concerning João Kuntz
subfiles.about: A cross-reference identifies information concerning João Kuntz in connection with SKF Industries.
subfiles.summary: João Kuntz is named as a person potentially connected with subversive activity. The note cites reference file 862.20210.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference concerning Kajsa Rothman
subfiles.about: A cross-reference directs users to information concerning Kajsa Rothman.
subfiles.summary: Kajsa Rothman is indexed in relation to possible subversive activity. The cited reference is file 800.20210.

subfiles.title: Case jackets: Alleged Japanese subversive activities of Tanji
subfiles.about: Duplicate jackets open a case on alleged Japanese subversive activities by a man named Tanji.
subfiles.summary: The covers identify Tanji, whose given name was unknown, as the subject of file 894.20200. The accompanying intelligence report concerns his activities in Tahiti.

subfiles.title: ONI intelligence report on Tanji in Tahiti
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Service; FBI; Department of State
subfiles.about: An intelligence report describes Tanji’s contacts with Japanese naval personnel and suspected work for the Japanese government.
subfiles.summary: ONI report: Tanji, a contractor and fisherman in French Tahiti for twenty-five years, reportedly entertained officers of visiting Japanese ships in 1940; an informant thought he worked for Japan.

subfiles.title: Passport Division memorandum concerning Ely Widler
subfiles.about: Ruth Shipley recommends supplying the FBI with information on Ely Widler from an attached file.
subfiles.summary: Shipley advises furnishing the FBI with the Department's file information on Ely Widler.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to the FBI concerning Ely Widler
subfiles.to: J. Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: A draft response states that a Department file search found no information on Ely Widler.
subfiles.summary: Draft reply to Hoover's October 19, 1944 communication: the Department's files had no information on Ely Widler.

subfiles.title: Final memorandum to the FBI concerning Ely Widler
subfiles.from: Adolf A. Berle, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.to: John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: The Department supplies the FBI with historical information about Ely Widler despite finding no passport record.
subfiles.summary: Final FBI memorandum: no passport for Ely Widler, but a 1944 report calls him a pro-Japanese Shanghai resident and a 1923 despatch records his arms-smuggling arrest in Sichuan.

subfiles.title: Case jackets: Alleged Japanese subversive activities of Serge Wittouck
subfiles.about: Duplicate jackets open a case on alleged Japanese subversive activities by Serge Wittouck.
subfiles.summary: The covers identify Brussels banker Serge Wittouck as the subject of file 894.20200. The following report connects him with oil-concession negotiations in Portuguese Timor.

subfiles.title: ONI intelligence report on Serge Wittouck
subfiles.to: FBI; Military Intelligence Service; Department of State
subfiles.about: An intelligence note reports suspicions that Serge Wittouck sought Portuguese Timor oil concessions for possible Japanese benefit.
subfiles.summary: ONI report on Brussels banker Serge Wittouck, who sought oil concessions on Portuguese Timor in 1939 and was reportedly friendly with Japanese interests.
